successCriteria.description: PgNotificationRepository implements all four methods of INotificationRepository (findByRecipientId, findByRecipientIdAndStatus, create, updateStatus) using parameterized SQL queries against the `notifications` table via the pg Pool from `src/shared/db/connection.ts`

PgNotificationRepository.create accepts an Omit<Notification, 'id' | 'createdAt'> input, INSERTs a row into the notifications table, and returns the created Notification with id and createdAt populated
PgNotificationRepository.updateStatus updates the status (and optionally readAt) of a notification row by id, returns the updated Notification, and returns null when no row matches the id

NotificationService implements all six methods of INotificationService (notifyLeaveSubmitted, notifyLeaveApproved, notifyLeaveRejected, notifyLeaveCancelled, getNotifications, markAsRead) and its constructor accepts an INotificationRepository

Each notify* method creates a Notification via the repository with the correct NotificationType, a non-empty title, a non-empty message, relatedEntityType set to 'leave_request', and relatedEntityId set to the leaveRequest.id from the argument

NotificationService.markAsRead delegates to repository.updateStatus with status NotificationStatus.read and sets readAt to the current timestamp; getNotifications delegates to repository.findByRecipientId

constraints: All database queries must use parameterized placeholders ($1, $2, …) — no string interpolation of user-supplied values into SQL
Repository must import the pg Pool from `src/shared/db/connection.ts` (not create its own pool or connection)
Repository must use a snake_case↔camelCase mapping pattern (mapRowToNotification function) consistent with PgBalanceRepository and PgAuditLogRepository

NotificationService must not import or depend on any leave-request implementation file — it only depends on notification.model.ts (which type-imports LeaveRequest) and the INotificationRepository interface
outOfScope: Unit/integration tests for notification.repository.ts and notification.service.ts — these are produced in Phase 3c: LeaveRequest Controller, Routes & All Tests
LeaveRequest repository, service, controller, routes — these are produced in sibling sub-phase 3b
Notification controller, routes, or any HTTP surface — the notification module has no controller/routes in this phase

ambiguities.description: The initial NotificationStatus for newly created notifications is not explicitly specified. The Notification entity requires a status field, and the create input is Omit<Notification, 'id' | 'createdAt'> — so status must be provided. The natural default is 'pending' (not yet delivered) or 'sent' (created and delivered).

entityInvariants.invariant: Every Notification must have a non-empty recipientId, a valid NotificationType, a non-empty title, a non-empty message, and a valid NotificationStatus. relatedEntityType and relatedEntityId are both set together or both null — never one without the other.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: none — repository layer has no auth; auth is enforced at the controller/middleware layer
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must propagate database errors (e.g. constraint violations) as rejected promises — no silent catch-and-swallow

interfaceConstraints.authRule: none at service layer — caller (controller) must enforce that the requesting user owns the notification
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must throw or propagate an error if the notification does not exist (repository returns null → service throws a domain error)

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Repository must follow the same snake_case↔camelCase mapping pattern as PgBalanceRepository (mapRowToBalance) and PgAuditLogRepository (mapRowToAuditLog) — define a NotificationRow interface and a mapRowToNotification function

NotificationService must match the INotificationService interface signatures exactly as declared in notification.model.ts — each notify* method accepts a LeaveRequest and returns Promise<Notification>, getNotifications accepts recipientId and returns Promise<Notification[]>, markAsRead accepts id and returns Promise<Notification>

The notifications table name and column names must match the reconciled architecture: table `notifications` with columns id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at

integrationPoints.target: src/shared/db/connection.ts — the pg Pool instance (named `pool`) used by all repository implementations
integrationPoints.why: PgNotificationRepository must import and use this shared pool for all database operations

integrationPoints.target: src/modules/notification/notification.model.ts — the Notification entity, INotificationRepository, and INotificationService interfaces
integrationPoints.why: Both PgNotificationRepository and NotificationService must import and satisfy these interfaces exactly
